answer.rationale: memory_c2 is the load-bearing memory here: it is the only record that would justify moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor, and the current low-cost quote meets the 18% mandate alone, so the cost pressure points straight at it. That makes it the memory most worth spending the single verification pull on. What the consolidated summary does not tell me is the context that matters now: what volume and criticality that prior switch covered, whether the line had buffer at the time, how long onboarding actually took in calendar days, and whether delivery reliability (not just invoicing accuracy) was ever tested under load. 'Onboarding was quick and invoicing stayed accurate' is a narrow claim that could easily be read as a general endorsement of switching primary supply. Absent that detail, moving primary supply in 14 days while the line runs at 94% of committed volume with no buffer converts a pure cost problem into a delivery-risk problem, and the stated objective forbids that trade. Meanwhile memory_c4 (benchmarking moved the incumbent on both price and terms) offers a path to the mandate that does not touch continuity, and the low-cost quote is itself the benchmark that makes that negotiation credible. So I intend to negotiate with the incumbent against the low-cost quote, keeping the commitment short rather than immediately taking the multi-year volume discount from memory_c6, so that a verified switch or the second-source play in memory_c3 remains open at the next review. I am treating the inherited memories as generally reliable but noting they are all success records with no recorded failures, which is the signature of survivorship: the archive may simply not have retained the cases where a switch or a deferral went badly. Concretely, memory_c5's deferral is not portable here because this contract does not auto-renew, so deferring risks an actual supply gap rather than budget flexibility. Residual risk I am accepting: the incumbent may not close the full 18% gap, in which case the shortfall carries to the next review with a qualification trial of the low-cost vendor already scoped.
